summary: Food delivery, Instamart shopping, dining and experiences, supported by a wider supply-chain and technology business.
description: Swiggy coordinates restaurant ordering and delivery, quick-commerce fulfilment and out-of-home services. Its supply-chain business also serves merchants and brands. Several activities can use the same app without having the same revenue or cost model.
money: The group records revenue from the relevant platform fees, commissions, advertising, memberships, distribution and other commercial arrangements. Delivery, picking, warehousing, promotions, staff and technology affect what remains.
customers: Consumers order meals, groceries and experiences. Restaurants, merchants, wholesalers, retailers and consumer-goods businesses also use and pay for relevant services within the group.
drivers: Orders, active transacting users, basket value, partner terms, local fulfilment density, store maturity, discounts, delivery costs and funding for newer services.

groups.title: Food delivery
groups.examples: The restaurant marketplace and delivery service, with formats aimed at different convenience and affordability needs.
groups.explanation: A restaurant prepares the meal; the platform coordinates discovery, ordering, payments and delivery. Meal value is not all platform revenue.

groups.title: Instamart quick commerce
groups.examples: Groceries and household goods fulfilled through merchant and dark-store arrangements.
groups.explanation: Stock availability, local demand, picking and delivery can matter as much as the number of sites.

groups.title: Dining and experiences
groups.examples: Dineout and Scenes offerings under out-of-home consumption.
groups.explanation: Reservations, payments and event experiences differ from delivering goods, so their frequency and costs need separate reading.

groups.title: Supply chain and newer services
groups.examples: Warehousing, distribution and services for merchants and brands, plus incubated offerings.
groups.explanation: The supply-chain segment can record substantial goods-related revenue. New app features are not automatically separate profitable reporting segments.

basics.title: Gross order value and revenue have different owners
basics.text: The customer’s transaction includes amounts destined for restaurants, merchants and partners. The company recognises revenue under its own arrangements; it does not retain every amount collected at checkout.

basics.title: Breakeven depends on the cost boundary
basics.text: Contribution margin may exclude costs that adjusted EBITDA includes, while reported profit includes other expenses. Always ask which costs remain outside the stated breakeven claim.

steps.title: Create useful selection
steps.text: Bring users, restaurants and merchants into the relevant service.

steps.title: Receive an order
steps.text: Match demand to a restaurant, merchant, stock location or experience.

steps.title: Coordinate fulfilment
steps.text: Prepare or pick goods, arrange delivery or complete the dining transaction.

steps.title: Settle and fund operations
steps.text: Pay partners and operating costs while investing in service quality and growth.

specifics.title: Quick-commerce sites need a ramp-up period
specifics.text: A new dark store can add coverage before it achieves enough orders to support rent, stock handling, staff and delivery. Mature and recently opened sites should not be treated as identical.

specifics.title: Membership is part of the demand economics
specifics.text: Benefits can encourage users to transact across services, but the cost of those benefits and repeat use must be considered. A subscription sold is not proof that each related order earns money.

specifics.title: Business boundaries can change
specifics.text: Service formats, pilots and disposals change over time. Read the period’s segment notes and current announcements rather than treating every historic app feature or acquired activity as permanently present.

watch: Are orders and repeat usage improving sustainably?
Growth bought through incentives can behave differently from repeat demand.

Read active transacting customers, frequency, orders and average value alongside promotions. Check the exact service and period, and do not compare cumulative registered users with a monthly paying-user measure.
Are Instamart economics improving as stores mature?
Site openings and profitable fulfilment are different outcomes.

Read orders, delivery and picking costs, store cohorts and expansion spending where disclosed. Check whether a cited margin is contribution, adjusted EBITDA or the statutory segment result; they are not interchangeable.
What does each business actually earn?
Large revenue can come from low-margin distribution.

Read food delivery, out-of-home, quick commerce, supply chain and innovation results separately. Keep negative rows visible and use external-customer revenue after internal adjustments rather than adding overlapping headline measures.
Do restaurant and delivery relationships remain workable?
Service quality and partner terms influence demand and costs.

Read partner availability, fulfilment quality and relevant regulatory or official disclosures. Higher platform fees may improve revenue but can also affect consumer choice, restaurant relationships and competitive response.
Can the group fund its expansion and newer offerings?
Operating losses and capital spending use cash.

Compare the bridge from adjusted measures to reported earnings, operating cash flow, leases and investment. Check any disposal or restructuring before assuming that a past business’s revenue will recur.
risks: Discounts and service competition can hold back earnings.
Poor fulfilment, merchant availability or stock handling can weaken repeat demand.
New sites and service experiments can consume cash before reaching scale.
Labour, food safety, consumer protection, data and contractual issues can affect operating costs or continuity.
context: One app contains several operating models

The official business directory describes restaurant food delivery, merchant fulfilment and dining solutions separately. The experience may feel unified to a user, while the financial statements have to distinguish the underlying activities.
quiz: Does a profitable food-delivery business guarantee that the group is profitable?
No. Losses in quick commerce or other activities and company-level expenses can outweigh a positive business result. Read the full table and its reconciliation.
sources: FY26 shareholder letter and segment definitions

financialNotes.title: The existing table uses the financial statement’s measure
financialNotes.text: It preserves external revenue after inter-segment adjustments and the reported segment result. Adjusted EBITDA and gross order value must not be substituted into those columns.

financialNotes.title: Read the losses as part of the business story
financialNotes.text: The verified snapshot shows different outcomes across food delivery, out-of-home, quick commerce, supply chain and innovations. Segment results still require the source’s reconciliation for other income, share-based payments, finance, depreciation and other items before group net profit.
